In [[geometry]], the '''cyclotruncated simplicial honeycomb''' (or '''cyclotruncated n-simplex honeycomb''') is a dimensional infinite series of [[Honeycomb (geometry)|honeycomb]]s, based on the symmetry of the <math>{\tilde{A}}_n</math> affine [[Coxeter group]]. It is given a [[Schläfli symbol]] t<sub>0,1</sub>{3<sup>[n+1]</sup>}, and is represented by a [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]] as a cyclic graph of ''n+1'' nodes with two adjacent nodes ringed. It is composed of n-[[simplex]] facets, along with all [[Truncation (geometry)|truncated]] n-simplices.

It is also called a '''[[Kagome lattice]]''' in two and three dimensions, although it is not a lattice.

In n-dimensions, each can be seen as a set of ''n+1'' sets of parallel [[hyperplane]]s that divide space. Each hyperplane contains the same honeycomb of one dimension lower.

In 1-dimension, the honeycomb represents an [[apeirogon]], with alternately colored [[line segment]]s. In 2-dimensions, the honeycomb represents the [[trihexagonal tiling]], with Coxeter graph {{CDD|branch_11|split2|node}}. In 3-dimensions it represents the [[quarter cubic honeycomb]], with Coxeter graph {{CDD|branch_11|3ab|branch}} filling space with alternately tetrahedral and truncated tetrahedral cells. In 4-dimensions it is called a [[cyclotruncated 5-cell honeycomb]], with Coxeter graph {{CDD|branch_11|3ab|nodes|split2|node}}, with [[5-cell]], [[truncated 5-cell]], and [[bitruncated 5-cell]] facets. In 5-dimensions it is called a [[cyclotruncated 5-simplex honeycomb]], with Coxeter graph {{CDD|branch_11|3ab|nodes|3ab|branch}}, filling space by [[5-simplex]], [[truncated 5-simplex]], and [[bitruncated 5-simplex]] facets. In 6-dimensions it is called a [[cyclotruncated 6-simplex honeycomb]], with Coxeter graph {{CDD|branch_11|3ab|nodes|3ab|nodes|split2|node}}, filling space by [[6-simplex]], [[truncated 6-simplex]], [[bitruncated 6-simplex]], and [[tritruncated 6-simplex]] facets.

== Projection by folding ==

The cyclotruncated (2''n''+1)- and 2''n''-simplex honeycombs and (2''n''−1)-simplex honeycombs can be projected into the n-dimensional [[hypercubic honeycomb]] by a [[Coxeter–Dynkin diagram#Geometric folding|geometric folding]] operation that maps two pairs of mirrors into each other, sharing the same [[vertex arrangement]]:
